questions.text: As per the table below showing Budget Estimates (BE) 2024-25 for Major Subsidies (in Rs Lakh Crore), what is the approximate percentage share of Food Subsidy in the total Major Subsidies? | Subsidy Type | Allocation (Rs Lakh Crore) | | :--- | :--- | | Food Subsidy | 2.05 | | Fertilizer Subsidy | 1.64 | | Petroleum Subsidy | 0.12 | | **Total Major Subsidies** | **3.81** |
questions.solution: Shortcut: Approximate the fraction 2.05/3.81. Round to 2.0/3.8 = 20/38 = 10/19. Since 10/20 = 50%, and denominator is slightly smaller (19), the value is slightly above 50%. Only 54% fits. Step-by-step: Total Major Subsidies = 3.81 Lakh Cr. Food Subsidy = 2.05 Lakh Cr. Percentage = (2.05 / 3.81) * 100. Calculate 2.05/3.81 ≈ 0.538. 0.538 * 100 = 53.8% ≈ 54%.

questions.text: Consider the following statements regarding the National Green Tribunal (NGT): 1. It is a specialized body set up to expeditiously deal with environmental related litigation. 2. The head of the NGT is known as the Chairperson, who is appointed by the President of India. 3. The decisions of the NGT are not subject to appeal in any court of law. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution: Statement 1 is correct as the NGT was established under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 to handle environmental disputes quickly. Statement 2 is correct; the Chairperson of the NGT is appointed by the President of India. Statement 3 is incorrect because Section 14 of the NGT Act allows for appeals to be filed directly to the Supreme Court of India against any order or decision of the Tribunal.

questions.text: As per the table below showing the Forest Cover in the top three states and the Total Forest Cover of India as per the India State of Forest Report (ISFR) 2021, what is the approximate percentage share of these three states combined in India's total Forest Cover? | State | Forest Cover (sq km) | | :--- | :--- | | Madhya Pradesh | 77,483 | | Arunachal Pradesh | 66,431 | | Chhattisgarh | 55,717 | | **India (Total)** | **7,13,789** |
questions.solution: Shortcut: Sum top 3 states ≈ 77.5 + 66.4 + 55.7 = 199.6 thousand sq km. Total = 713.8 thousand. % = 199.6 / 713.8. Approximate 200/714 ≈ 100/357 ≈ 28%. Option Elimination: 10% of Total is ~71.4. 199.6 is between 2×71.4 (142.8) and 3×71.4 (214.2). Closer to 3rd multiple → ~28%. Step-by-step: 1. Combined Forest Cover of three states = 77,483 + 66,431 + 55,717 = 1,99,631 sq km. 2. Total Forest Cover of India = 7,13,789 sq km. 3. Percentage = (1,99,631 / 7,13,789) × 100 = 27.96% ≈ 28%.

questions.text: Arrange the following major events of the Indian National Movement in correct chronological order: 1. Jallianwala Bagh Massacre 2. Launch of Non-Cooperation Movement 3. Dandi March (Salt Satyagraha) 4. Launch of Quit India Movement Select the correct sequence using the code given below:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Elimination by anchor dates. Jallianwala Bagh (1919) is the earliest event. Non-Cooperation (1920) follows immediately. Dandi March (1930) is a decade later. Quit India (1942) is the last. Only Option A satisfies the sequence 1919 → 1920 → 1930 → 1942. Full Solution: 1. Jallianwala Bagh Massacre occurred on April 13, 1919. 2. Non-Cooperation Movement was launched in September 1920. 3. Dandi March commenced on March 12, 1930. 4. Quit India Movement was launched on August 8, 1942. The correct chronological order is 1-2-3-4.

questions.text: As per the table below showing Literacy Rates (Census 2011) for four major states, which state has the highest absolute difference (Gender Gap) between Male and Female Literacy Rates? | State | Male Literacy (%) | Female Literacy (%) | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Rajasthan | 79.19 | 52.12 | | Bihar | 71.20 | 51.50 | | Uttar Pradesh | 77.28 | 57.18 | | Madhya Pradesh | 78.73 | 59.24 |
questions.solution: Shortcut: Calculate gaps mentally using approximation/unit digits. Rajasthan: 79.2 - 52.1 = 27.1. Bihar: 71.2 - 51.5 = 19.7. UP: 77.3 - 57.2 = 20.1. MP: 78.7 - 59.2 = 19.5. Rajasthan (27.1%) is clearly the highest. Option Elimination: Bihar, UP, MP gaps are ~20%; Rajasthan gap is ~27%. Step-by-step: 1. Rajasthan Gap = 79.19 - 52.12 = 27.07%. 2. Bihar Gap = 71.20 - 51.50 = 19.70%. 3. UP Gap = 77.28 - 57.18 = 20.10%. 4. MP Gap = 78.73 - 59.24 = 19.49%. 5. Highest Gap = Rajasthan (27.07%).

questions.text: As per the table below showing the geographical area of four major Indian states (in lakh sq km) and India's total geographical area (32.87 lakh sq km), which state's area constitutes approximately 10% of the country's total area? | State | Area (Lakh sq km) | | :--- | :--- | | Rajasthan | 3.42 | | Madhya Pradesh | 3.08 | | Maharashtra | 3.07 | | Uttar Pradesh | 2.41 |
questions.solution: Shortcut: Calculate 10% of India's total area (32.87) by shifting decimal: 3.287 lakh sq km. Scan the 'Area' column for the value closest to 3.29. Rajasthan (3.42) is the nearest; others are ~3.07 or lower. Full Solution: 10% of 32.87 lakh sq km = 3.287 lakh sq km. Comparing state areas: Rajasthan (3.42), Madhya Pradesh (3.08), Maharashtra (3.07), Uttar Pradesh (2.41). The absolute difference for Rajasthan is |3.42 - 3.287| = 0.133. For Madhya Pradesh, it is |3.08 - 3.287| = 0.207. Rajasthan is the closest.

questions.text: As per the table below showing Installed Renewable Energy Capacity (excluding Large Hydro) as of March 31, 2024 (in GW), what is the approximate percentage share of Solar Power in the total Renewable Capacity (excluding Large Hydro)? | Source | Capacity (GW) | | :--- | :--- | | Solar Power | 81.8 | | Wind Power | 45.9 | | Bio Power | 10.4 | | Small Hydro Power | 5.0 | | **Total (Excl. Large Hydro)** | **143.1** |
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use approximation 82/143. Simplify: 80/140 = 8/14 = 4/7. 4/7 ≈ 57.1%. Option 57% is the closest. Step-by-step: Total Capacity (Excl Large Hydro) = 143.1 GW. Solar Capacity = 81.8 GW. Percentage = (81.8 / 143.1) * 100. 81.8/143.1 ≈ 0.5716. 0.5716 * 100 = 57.16% ≈ 57%.

questions.text: As per the table below showing Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) in usual status (ps+ss) for persons aged 15 years and above as per the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) 2023-24, which category exhibits the highest absolute gender gap (difference between Male and Female LFPR in percentage points)?

options.label: D
options.text: The gap is equal across all categories

questions.solution: **Shortcut (Conceptual Elimination):** Male LFPR is relatively stable across Rural (~79.5%) and Urban (~77.2%) areas. However, Female LFPR differs drastically: Rural females participate significantly more (~47.6%) due to agricultural/allyied engagement, while Urban female participation is very low (~28.0%). Since Gap = Male % - Female %, the gap is widest where Female % is lowest. Urban Female LFPR (28.0%) < All India Female LFPR (41.7%) < Rural Female LFPR (47.6%). Therefore, Urban Gap > All India Gap > Rural Gap. Select **Urban**. **Worked Solution:** 1. **Rural Gap** = 79.5 - 47.6 = **31.9 percentage points** 2. **Urban Gap** = 77.2 - 28.0 = **49.2 percentage points** 3. **All India Gap** = 78.8 - 41.7 = **37.1 percentage points** Comparing the gaps: 49.2 (Urban) > 37.1 (All India) > 31.9 (Rural). The highest gap is in the **Urban** category.

questions.text: As per the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) 2022-23 annual report, the estimated distribution of workers by broad industry division is shown below. What is the approximate percentage point difference between the share of workers in 'Agriculture' and 'Services' sectors? | Sector | Percentage of Workers | | :--- | :--- | | Agriculture | 45.8 | | Manufacturing | 12.6 | | Construction | 13.0 | | Services | 28.6 |
questions.solution: Shortcut: Round the percentages to nearest integers (46% and 29%) and subtract mentally: 46 - 29 = 17. This approximation avoids decimal subtraction and matches option B exactly. Full Solution: The exact shares are Agriculture (45.8%) and Services (28.6%). The difference is 45.8 - 28.6 = 17.2 percentage points. The closest approximation among the options is 17 percentage points.

questions.text: As per the table below showing Budget Estimates (BE) 2023-24 for four major Central Government schemes (in Rs Lakh Crore), what is the approximate percentage share of PM Awas Yojana in the total allocation for these four schemes? | Scheme | Allocation (Rs Lakh Cr) | | :--- | :--- | | MGNREGA | 0.60 | | PM-KISAN | 0.60 | | Jal Jeevan Mission | 0.70 | | PM Awas Yojana | 0.79 |
questions.solution: **Shortcut (Approximation & Fraction Simplification):** Round allocations: 0.6, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8. Total ≈ 2.7. Target = 0.8. Fraction = 0.8 / 2.7 = 8/27. Since 27 × 3 = 81, 8/27 ≈ 29.6% (close to 30%). Option C (29.5%) is closest. **Step-by-Step:** 1. Calculate Total Allocation = 0.60 + 0.60 + 0.70 + 0.79 = 2.69 Lakh Cr. 2. PM Awas Allocation = 0.79 Lakh Cr. 3. Percentage = (0.79 / 2.69) × 100. 4. Simplify: 79 / 269 ≈ 0.2936. 5. 0.2936 × 100 = 29.36% ≈ 29.5%.

questions.text: As per the recommendations of the 15th Finance Commission (for the award period 2021-26), what is the share of States in the net proceeds of Union taxes (Vertical Devolution)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Recall the specific figure for 15th FC (41%) vs 14th FC (42%). The 1% reduction was due to the creation of UTs of J&K and Ladakh. Option B (41%) is the standard cited figure for 15th FC vertical devolution. Full Solution: The 15th Finance Commission (Chairman N.K. Singh) recommended a vertical devolution of 41% of the divisible pool of taxes to the States for the period 2021-26, a 1 percentage point decrease from the 42% recommended by the 14th Finance Commission.

questions.text: As per the table below showing the Gross Value Added (GVA) at basic prices by economic activity for a hypothetical year (in Rs Lakh Crore), what is the approximate percentage share of the 'Services' sector in the total GVA? | Sector | GVA (Rs Lakh Crore) | | :--- | :--- | | Agriculture & Allied | 22.5 | | Industry | 31.0 | | Services | 58.5 |
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use approximation. Total ≈ 22.5 + 31 + 58.5 = 112. Services share = 58.5/112. Note 58.5 is slightly more than half of 112 (which is 56). 58.5/112 ≈ 52.2%. Option B (52%) is closest. Full Solution: Total GVA = 22.5 + 31.0 + 58.5 = 112.0 Lakh Crore. Percentage = (58.5 / 112.0) × 100 = 52.23% ≈ 52%.

questions.text: As per the table below showing the Horizontal Devolution Criteria and Weights recommended by the 15th Finance Commission (for 2021-26), which criterion has been assigned the highest weight? | Criterion | Weight (%) | | :--- | :--- | | Population (2011) | 15.0 | | Area | 15.0 | | Forest and Ecology | 10.0 | | Income Distance | 45.0 | | Demographic Performance | 12.5 | | Tax Effort | 2.5 |
questions.solution: Shortcut: Visual Scan / Magnitude Comparison. The weights are 15, 15, 10, 45, 12.5, 2.5. The largest number is 45.0 corresponding to Income Distance. No calculation needed, pure option elimination based on magnitude. Step-by-step: 1. List weights: Population=15%, Area=15%, Forest=10%, Income Distance=45%, Demographic Performance=12.5%, Tax Effort=2.5%. 2. Identify maximum value: 45%. 3. Match criterion: Income Distance.

questions.text: As per the table below showing the Budget Estimates (BE) 2024-25 for Gross Tax Revenue (in Rs Lakh Crore), what is the approximate percentage share of Direct Taxes in the total Gross Tax Revenue? | Tax Component | Amount (Rs Lakh Crore) | | :--- | :--- | | Corporation Tax | 10.43 | | Income Tax | 11.87 | | Customs | 2.33 | | Union Excise Duties | 3.22 | | GST | 9.68 | | Others | 0.47 |
questions.solution: Shortcut: Direct Taxes = Corp Tax + Income Tax = 10.43 + 11.87 = 22.30. Indirect Taxes ≈ 2.33 + 3.22 + 9.68 + 0.47 = 15.70. Total ≈ 38.00. % Direct = 22.3/38 ≈ 58.7% → ~58%. Use 10% anchor: 10% of 38 is 3.8. 22.3 is approx 5.8 × 3.8 → 58%. Step-by-step: 1. Sum Direct Taxes: 10.43 + 11.87 = 22.30 Lakh Cr. 2. Sum Indirect Taxes: 2.33 + 3.22 + 9.68 + 0.47 = 15.70 Lakh Cr. 3. Total Gross Tax Revenue = 22.30 + 15.70 = 38.00 Lakh Cr. 4. Percentage = (22.30 / 38.00) × 100 = 58.68% ≈ 58%.

questions.text: Under Article 368 of the Constitution of India, which of the following categories of amendments requires ratification by the Legislatures of not less than one-half of the States?

options.label: A
options.text: Election of the President of India

options.label: B
options.text: Extent of the executive power of the Union and the States

questions.solution: Shortcut: Article 368 proviso lists specific federal provisions requiring state ratification. If a candidate identifies that even two of the listed options (e.g., Election of President and Representation of States) are entrenched federal provisions, 'All of the above' becomes the logical choice without verifying the third. Full Solution: Article 368 stipulates that amendments to provisions affecting the federal structure (listed in the proviso) require special majority of Parliament plus ratification by half the State Legislatures. The list explicitly includes: (a) Articles 54 and 55 (Election of President); (b) Articles 73 and 162 (Extent of executive power); (c) Chapter IV of Part V, Chapter V of Part VI, Chapter I of Part XI (Judiciary, Legislative Relations); (d) Any of the Lists in Seventh Schedule; (e) Representation of States in Parliament; (f) Proviso to Article 368 itself. Since all three options (A, B, C) are explicitly mentioned in the proviso to Article 368, option D is correct.
